name: Atsam
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Ayandipo, Omotola Islamiyat. 2011. Aspects of phonology of Atsam language. BA long essay, University of Ilorin, 83 pp. -- chapter one and full table of contents as republished (unattributed) on iproject.com.ng, projectclue.com and researchwap.com.
sources.access_detail: read online, no file saved; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Accessible part (ch. 1 + TOC) says nothing about stress. TOC shows ch. 2 'Tone inventory of Atsam' p. 37, 'Syllable inventory of Atsam' p. 39, and ch. 4 'Atsam tonological and syllable processes' pp. 58-66 (Defining a tone language; Atsam tone typology; Co-occurrence of tones; Function of tones; Tone spreading/stability/floating; syllable structure). No stress heading anywhere. Body of ch. 2-4 not accessible (host paywall; Hammarström holds a scan, hh file). Saved HTML/TXT of the accessible pages:,.

sources.citation: Akangbe, Moriike Oluwatoyin. 2011. Negation in Atsam (Chawai) language. BA long essay, University of Ilorin, 101 pp. -- chapter one as republished on iproject.com.ng; abstract page on samphina.com.ng.
sources.access_detail: read online, no file saved; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing on tone or stress in the accessible chapter one.

Tertiary, machine-written: asserts 'Atsam is a tone language featuring high, mid, and low tones... tone spreading and floating' and CV syllables; no source given for the claim (appears derived from the Ayandipo 2011 TOC); says nothing about stress. Not citable.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2020. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 45-92. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.210 (open access).
sources.note: Nothing. Tsam (=Chawai) appears only in the status table (source: Ajaegbu et al. 2013 SIL survey ms), the classification tree and one lexical table; the phonology section describes Boze (3 level tones + superhigh, glides). No word on Atsam/Tsam stress or tone.

sources.citation: Watters, John R. (ed.) 2018. East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs (Niger-Congo Comparative Studies 1). Berlin: Language Science Press (incl. Blench, ch. 3 'Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages').
sources.note: Nothing; Tsam (=Cahwai [sic]) appears only in the East Kainji tree, p. 83.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2012 ms. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria: state of the art. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, 12 pp. (Wayback copy of rogerblench.info).
sources.note: Nothing on Atsam; notes Meek 1931 wordlist of Atsam and that 'Atsam (Chawai) and Piti are somewhat different from the others'; phonology section is about Boze tones.
